# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-10 (Extended v97)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring-Summer Year 3, dual settings)**: (1) Paris, le Petit-Picpus convent district—Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary within walled convent garden; (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton) and Vernon with multiple inhabitants. **Environmental conditions (Spring-Summer Year 3)**: roads rutted and puddled after thaw; frost silvered hedges; bees hummed in lavender; children chased hoops; dogs barked sporadically; bell for vespers rang thinly; light went early; smoke lay flat over fields; gulls quarreled over fish heads by harbor steps; wind came off water with salt/tar smell. **Population movements (English locations)**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton; Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged; Luena packed trunk, moved Staveford to Dungate; Rozek Stenenridge followed within month; Volan Stenworth (now Peten) mended sleeve by window, said little; Ismira Stenson made observations about weather/harvest with Matho Stenson (aching back); Ismira bought ribbon at stall and regretted it; **Ismira claimed Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (no body seen)**. **Dunstead granary fire**: Ismira told Luena fire was set on purpose (claim/rumor).

## Primary Locations

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (convent carriage gate). **Convent complex—three buildings**: (1) Great Convent (Bernardines-Benedictines nuns); (2) Boarding-school; (3) Little Convent (aged nuns of various orders). **Interior garden**: Vast oblong with poplar alley, forest trees, gnarled fruit-tree, vegetable beds, melon patch, old well, stone benches. **Chapel**: Window visible from garden. **Burial location**: Mother Crucifixion's vault beneath grand altar (concealed). **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient burial ground with Prefecture Permission for nightfall interments; grave-digger Father Mestienne (deceased); replaced by "little Father Lenoir."

**ENGLISH PROVINCIAL SETTINGS**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton; market towns with parsonages, forges, granaries, ovens, wells, lanes.

**VERNON**: Colonel Pontmercy's residence (smallest house he could find); reached from Paris by diligence from Rue du Bouloi passing through Vernon at night.

**GORBEAU HOVEL (50-52)**: Salpêtrière district, outskirts Paris. Posted "Chambers to let"; presently inhabited by indigent individuals. **Current tenant—Jondrette family**: Father hired chamber, stated name upon hiring; instructed portress to respond affirmatively if inquired for Pole, Italian, or Spaniard.

**M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Formerly **Rue Servandoni**; maintained **Rue Férou residence** (frequented Madame de T.'s salon twice weekly from 1817 onward); **newly established Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire in the Marais** (after conclusion of Marius's classical studies). Doors absolutely closed during day; opens evenings after five o'clock dinner.

**MADAME DE T.'S SALON (Rue Férou house)**: **Madame la Baronne de T.**, worthy respectable person; husband Baron de T. was Ambassador to Berlin under Louis XVI (died bankrupt during emigration). Purely Royalist salon; twice-weekly assemblies; tea, horror at century/charter/Bonapartists, whispered hopes from Monsieur (Charles X). **Two cocks**: M. Gillenormand and Comte de Lamothe-Valois. Essence of white Parisian society; superior taste, exquisite, haughty. Old régime language customs seemed eccentric. Titles: _Madame la Générale_, _Madame la Colonelle_ (Madame de Léon, Marquise de Créquy).

## Jean Valjean's Development

**CURRENT STATUS (Spring-Summer Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works daily; pruner of trees; budded ungrafted orchard trees. Receives daily visits from Cosette (appointed hour); watches her running/playing; distinguishes her laugh. **Spiritual transformation**: Meditations; blood ran cold at grateful nuns' songs—realized he justly chastified while wretch shook fist at God. Scaled wall made to escape other expiation now served entrance to sanctuary. Pride vanished; scrutinized heart; wept. All recent months led back to Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Knelt in garden walks at eventide; prostrated in prayer. Soul became compounded of silence, perfume, simplicity, joy. Two houses of God received him critically: first when society rejected; second when society pursued. Without first, relapsed into crime; without second, into torment.

## Cosette's Development

**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Unhappiness trained silence. Hardly regained confidence with Valjean. **Convent integration**: Speedily accustomed; regretted Catherine but dared not say. Told Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away." Thinks herself his daughter. Became convent scholar; received pupil garb. Valjean restored mourning suit from Thénardier departure; locked up garments plus stockings/shoes with camphor/aromatics in valise on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?" At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind.

## Fauchelevent's Role

**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour traversing short distances; complains aching back.

**EXECUTION**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket with deaf fruit-seller (Rue Chemin-Vert). Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery. Grave-digger Father Mestienne dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Fauchelevent found lost card, buried corpse, filled grave himself.

**CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives good wine. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening; sole person aware of full presence; only known ally/protector. Nuns do not suspect him; eyes fixed on God do not spy.

## Javert's Pursuit

**REASSIGNMENT AND INVESTIGATION**: Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape (January 1823). Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter.

**SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. Reasons for secrecy: (1) Indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen.

**PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman warned Javert lodger intended to leave; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **Escape from Mouffetard**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades; sure convict could not be far off.

## M. Gillenormand and His World

**IDENTITY AND CHARACTER**: Worthy bourgeois; "consideration of absolutely first-rate quality"; dignified, honest, lofty in bourgeois fashion; great age added venerable dishevelment. Took prizes at College of Moulins (crowned by Duc de Nivernais). Received in aristocratic salons despite bourgeois birth. **Witticisms**: When King of Prussia visited as "Count de Ruppin," approved: "All kings who are not King of France are provincial kings." When asked _Courrier Français_ editor's sentence: "To be suspended. '_Sus_ is superfluous.'" Never went anywhere except on condition of being chief person. Oracle everywhere. Spoke with genuine sparkle of old rock.

**TWO DAUGHTERS**: Born ten years apart; little resemblance in youth. **Youngest** (Marius's mother): Charming soul turned towards light, occupied with flowers, verses, music; ethereal; wedded to vague heroic figure; died 1815, leaving child. **Eldest** (Mademoiselle Gillenormand): Over forty, looked fifty; antique virtue, incombustible prude; sharpest noses, most obtuse minds. Outside family, no one knew first name. Belonged to society of Virgin; wore white veil on festivals. Revered "holy blood," venerated "sacred heart"; contemplated rococo-jesuit altar hours. Chapel friend: ancient virgin Mademoiselle Vaubois (positive blockhead). Years wore away angles; softening came. Melancholy with obscure sadness. Never malicious (relative kindness); ermine of stupidity without single spot intelligence. Kept house for father; household of old man and old spinster touching aspect of two weaknesses leaning for support. **Servants**: Chambermaid Nicolette (succeeded to Magnon); short-breathed pursy Basque; porter.

## Marius Pontmercy: Background and Current Development

**PARENTAGE AND EARLY YEARS**: Son of Colonel Pontmercy (chief of squadron, meagre half-pay); mother Madame Pontmercy (née Gillenormand, youngest daughter—"admirable woman in every sense, lofty in sentiment and rare"). **1815**: Pontmercy married Mademoiselle Gillenormand between two wars; old M. Gillenormand gave consent with sigh. Mother died 1815, leaving child. Colonel's joy in solitude; grandfather imperatively claimed grandson, declaring if child not given would disinherit. Father yielded in child's interest; transferred his love to flowers. Colonel lives alone at Vernon (smallest house he could find); has meagre half-pay.

**CURRENT STATUS AND EDUCATION** (Age 7, Spring-Summer Year 3): Grandfather kept no relations with son-in-law (colonel "a bandit" to him); colonel called "brigand of the Loire." Never mentioned except with mocking allusions. **Expressly agreed**: Pontmercy never attempt to see or speak to son under penalty of disinheritance. For Gillenormands, Pontmercy man afflicted with plague. Grandfather intended to bring up child in own way. Colonel wrong perhaps to accept conditions, but submitted, thinking he did right, sacrificing no one but himself.

**INHERITANCE**: Father Gillenormand's inheritance not much; Mademoiselle Gillenormand the elder's inheritance considerable. This aunt, unmarried, very rich on maternal side; boy's natural heir. Boy's name Marius; knew he had father but nothing more.

**SECRET PATERNAL VISITS**: Colonel slipped away every two or three months, came to Paris secretly like criminal, posted himself at Saint-Sulpice at hour when Aunt Gillenormand led Marius to mass. There, trembling lest aunt turn round, concealed behind pillar, motionless, not daring breathe, gazed at child. Scarred veteran afraid of old spinster.

**CORRESPONDENCE**: Twice yearly (January 1st, St. George's day), Marius wrote duty letters dictated by aunt, pronounced copied from formula. Father answered with tender letters grandfather thrust into pocket unread.

**CLASSICAL STUDIES CONCLUSION**: Coincided with M. Gillenormand's departure from society. Old man bade farewell to Faubourg Saint-Germain and Madame de T.'s salon; established himself in Marais, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire.

**SUMMONS TO VERNON**: Marius seized with trembling fit upon notification to see father. Thought of everything except this. Forcing estrangement into reconciliation. Believed father did not love him (abandoned him to others). Convinced father "the slasher" (M. Gillenormand's amiable appellation) did not love him. Feeling not beloved, did not love. "Nothing is more simple," he said to himself. Crushed letter, thrust into pocket.

**JOURNEY TO VERNON**: Could have set out that evening; diligence from Rue du Bouloi took trip to Rouen by night, passed through Vernon. Neither Marius nor M. Gillenormand thought of making inquiries about it. Next day, at twilight, Marius reached Vernon. Asked first person for "M. Pontmercy's house." In his own mind, agreed with Restoration, did not recognize father's claim to title of colonel or baron.

**COLONEL'S DEATH**: Colonel attacked by brain fever three days previously. Foreboding of evil at illness beginning; written to M. Gillenormand demanding son. Malady grown worse. On very evening of Marius's arrival at Vernon, colonel had attack of delirium; rose from bed despite servant's efforts, crying: "My son is not coming! I shall go to meet him!" Ran out of room, fell prostrate on floor of antechamber. Had just expired.

## Narrative Themes and Commentary

**AUDACITY AND REVOLUTION**: All sublime conquests are prizes of daring. Necessary that Danton dare; cry "Audacity!" is "Fiat lux." Daring deeds dazzle history.

**BOURGEOIS HONOR**: In bourgeoisie, honored situations decay through too easy relations. One must beware whom one admits. Loss of caloric in vicinity of cold mirrors diminution of consideration in approach of despised persons.

**ULTRAMONTANE SOCIETY COMMENTARY**: To be ultra is to go beyond. Attack sceptre in name of throne, mitre in name of altar; ill-treat thing dragged; kick over traces; cavil at fagot on score of cooking received by heretics; reproach idol with small amount idolatry. Discover Pope not sufficiently papish, King not sufficiently royal, night has too much light. Discontented with alabaster, snow, swan, lily in name of whiteness. Partisan of things to point of becoming enemy. So strongly for, as to be against.

**SALON POLITICS AND LITERATURE**: Salons had literature and politics of own. Believed in Fiévée; M. Agier laid down law; commentated M. Colnet (old bookseller, Quay Malaquais). Napoleon thoroughly "Corsican Ogre." Later introduction of "M. le Marquis de Bonaparte, Lieutenant-General of King's armies" concession to spirit of age.

**RESPECT FOR PAST**: Author encountered curious moment of contemporary history; forced to cast passing glance, trace singular features of society unknown today. Does it rapidly without bitter/derisive idea. Souvenirs both respectful and affectionate touch his mother, attach him to this past. Same petty world had grandeur of its own. One may smile at it, neither despise nor hate. It was France of former days.
